issues.description: Field mismatch for Animal.name: In problem_statement.md the UML specification declares the Animal attribute as "- name: String" (problem_statement.md line 28). However, the textual instructions in the same problem statement (Part 1) explicitly require using a StringBuilder for the name attribute to enable efficient string manipulations (problem_statement.md line 85). The reference implementation in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java defines the field as `private String name;` (line 4). This three-way inconsistency (UML vs textual requirement vs solution) will confuse students about which type to implement, which getter/setter signatures to provide, and whether tests or provided code expect String or StringBuilder.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and reference implementation consistent. Option A (preferred if the course goal is to teach StringBuilder): update the UML in problem_statement.md to show `name: StringBuilder`, update the reference solution and any tests to store the name as a StringBuilder (e.g., `private StringBuilder name;`), initialize it in the constructor (`this.name = new StringBuilder(nameParam);`), and clarify whether getName() should return String (name.toString()) or a StringBuilder. Option B (preferred if simplicity and backward compatibility are desired): remove the StringBuilder requirement from the textual instructions and keep the UML and solution using `String`. Apply the chosen change consistently to problem_statement.md, the solution code, and any tests or example code in the template so students receive a single, unambiguous requirement.
